characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/Max-2200 X-ray Diffractometer, Cu target operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, graphite monochromator, λ = 0.154056 nm
characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel strips mainly consist of austenite and ferrite (retained high-temperature δ-ferrite). A double peak exists between 43.5° and 45.0° in the as-cast strips, identified as (110)δ and (220)DO3; the area ratio of the (110)δ peak to the (220)DO3 peak gradually decreases with increasing Cr content, indicating Cr promotes δ-ferrite → ordered DO3 transformation.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanning angle 30°–100°, continuous scanning at a speed of 4°/min
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase characterization of as-cast and annealed steel strips

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Phenom Pro SEM after mechanical polishing and etching; etching solution 3.3 vol% nitric acid + 3.3 vol% acetic acid + 0.1 vol% hydrofluoric acid, etching time 3 s; photographs taken 0.5 mm from the strip surface along the thickness direction
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributes in the γ-austenite matrix; Cr addition changes the short rod-shape ferrite into block ferrite. The volume fraction of δ-ferrite in the as-cast 3Cr strip is 12% (as-cast 0Cr 3%, 6Cr 18%).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; phase fraction averaged over ten different positions using Image-Pro Plus (IPP) image processing software
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the microstructure and measure the δ-ferrite volume fraction and morphology

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL-2010F operated at 200 kV; specimens prepared by twin-jet electrolytic polishing at −30 °C and 30 V with a mixed solution of 10% perchloric acid and 90% alcohol
characterization_methods.key_findings: The as-cast 3Cr strip consists of γ-austenite carrying a small κ-carbide fraction (weak (001) superlattice reflections; DF from (001) cannot resolve the precipitation) plus δ-ferrite containing nano-scale DO3 precipitates of size 30 ± 3 nm; measured lattice parameters of κ-carbides and γ-austenite are 0.387 nm and 0.376 nm, respectively.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SADP taken along the [110] zone axis
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the nano-scale precipitated phases (κ-carbides in γ-austenite, ordered DO3 in δ-ferrite)
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) with bright-field (BF) and dark-field (DF) imaging and selected-area diffraction patterns (SADP)

characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 3Cr: YS 642 ± 6 MPa, UTS 943 ± 10 MPa, TE 38 ± 3 %; the strain hardening rate gradually decreases during deformation with a weakened hump.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, constant strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1, gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm, in accordance with Chinese Standard GB/T-228.1-2010, at least 3 tests
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and total elongation and obtain stress-strain curves

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured average density of the 3Cr steel strip is 6.69 g/cm³ (0Cr 6.71 g/cm³, 6Cr 6.66 g/cm³).
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the average density of the steel strips

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP) and CS2800 carbon-sulfur analyzer
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured composition of the 3Cr steel (wt.%): Mn 20.04, Al 9.09, C 1.23, Cr 3.09, S 0.0009, Fe Bal. (Table 1).
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the chemical compositions of the steel strips
characterization_methods.technique: Chemical composition analysis (Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry and carbon-sulfur analysis)

interfaces.phase_evolution: The Cr element promotes the transformation from δ-ferrite to the ordered DO3 phase: the area ratio of the (110)δ peak to the (220)DO3 peak gradually decreases with increasing Cr content.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Effect of Cr addition on the as-cast strip: the as-cast 3Cr strip (YS 642 MPa) has significantly lower yield strength than the as-cast Cr-free (0Cr) strip (YS 836 MPa) while total elongation is not obviously changed; attributed to the decrease of nano-scale κ-carbides caused by Cr addition.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 100 g alloy ingot (Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-3Cr, wt.%) was prepared by melting 99.99% pure iron, 99.9% pure manganese, 99.9% pure aluminum, 99.9% pure chromium and 99.8% high-purity graphite by a cold-crucible levitation melting setup; the metal ingot was then remelted by induction melting.

The molten metal was poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm under near-rapid solidification in an argon atmosphere; as-cast steel strips with size 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm were obtained. This is the as-cast state of the 3Cr sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests performed at least 3 times using a MTS Criterion 44 Mechanical Property Tester
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm

strain_hardening_rate: As-cast 3Cr: Cr addition increases the strain hardening rate of the low-density steel strips; the hump present in the Cr-free steel becomes weak and the strain hardening rate gradually (monotonically) decreases during deformation.
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of the as-cast 3Cr steel strip (Fig. 3a/Fig. 2 last panel) and true stress-strain plus strain hardening rate curve of the as-cast 3Cr strip (Fig. 3c); 3Cr curve rises continuously beyond ~30% strain ending above 1000 MPa.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Measured by an AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer

phases_present.crystal_structure: lattice parameter 0.376 nm in the as-cast 3Cr steel strip

precipitates.distribution: Present in the γ-austenite; the (001) superlattice reflection intensity is so weak that the precipitation cannot be recognized in the DF image, indicating the volume fraction of κ-carbide decreases compared with the as-cast Cr-free (0Cr) strip.
precipitates.type: nano-scale κ-carbide (ideal stoichiometry (Fe, Mn)3AlC, perovskite crystal structure; lattice parameter 0.387 nm in as-cast 3Cr)

phases_present.crystal_structure: contains ordered DO3 phase (BCC, lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm)
phases_present.morphology: irregularly shaped/block δ-ferrite; the short rod-shape ferrite of the Cr-free steel changes into block ferrite with Cr addition

precipitates.distribution: densely distributed in the δ-ferrite (dark-field image using (002̄) shows densely distributed bright nanoparticles)
precipitates.type: ordered DO3 phase (BCC; lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm in the ferrite)

structures.number_of_phases: 2 main constituent phases (γ-austenite + δ-ferrite), plus nano-scale κ-carbides in austenite and ordered DO3 phase in ferrite
structures.overall_structure: Austenite-based duplex structure of the near-rapidly solidified as-cast 3Cr strip: irregularly shaped δ-ferrite (high-temperature δ-ferrite retained because of the high cooling rate during near-rapid solidification) distributed in a γ-austenite matrix, with nano-scale κ-carbides in the austenite and ordered DO3 phase in the δ-ferrite.

unmapped_findings: Measured composition of the as-cast 3Cr steel strip (Table 1, wt.%): Mn 20.04, Al 9.09, C 1.23, Cr 3.09, S 0.0009, Fe Bal.
UTS × TE product for the as-cast 3Cr steel strip: 35.8 GPa % (Table 2).
Measured lattice parameter of the κ-carbides and γ-austenite in the as-cast 3Cr steel strip is 0.387 nm and 0.376 nm, respectively.
The ordered DO3 phase is a body centered cubic crystal with a lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm in the ferrite (Fe or Mn atoms at corner positions, Al or Fe/Mn atoms at every other centered positions).
The ideal stoichiometry of the κ-carbide is (Fe, Mn)3AlC, which has a perovskite crystal structure (Fe/Mn at corners, Al at face centers, C at the cube center).

A double (Slip-band and Microband) hardening mechanism is proposed for the strain hardening behavior of the low-density steel strips: slip-band hardening acts at the early strain stage and microband hardening at the final strain stage; the number of nano-scale κ-carbides plays a crucial role in the strain hardening rate at the early strain stage.

For the as-cast 3Cr strip the κ-carbide volume fraction and average size are not explicitly reported; only that the volume fraction of κ-carbide decreases with Cr addition relative to the as-cast 0Cr strip (0Cr: 3%, 6 nm; annealed 0Cr: 7%, 8 nm; annealed 3Cr: 4%, 4 nm).
